data.title: Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Notches Up as Cybercabs Prove a Child-Free Environment
data.description:
Electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) may really be on to something with its Robotaxi system, the automated taxi system that allows users to basically input a destination and be driven there without human intervention. But it turns out that the Cybercabs that make part of the Robotaxi system are forbidden to anyone under the age of 13. This raises some unexpected issues, especially for families traveling in Cybercabs. But investors seemed reasonably pleased, based on the fractional boost in Tesla shares seen in Tuesday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 14.86% loss in its share price over the past year.

No Kids Allowed

The rules governing children in Cybercabs are a bit odd, and actually depend on what model said children will be traveling in. For Cybercabs themselves, no one under 13 is allowed at all. Those aged 13 to 17 are allowed, but an adult must be physically present for the entire trip. Meanwhile, children as young as eight are permitted in the Model Y vehicles that make up the rest of the Robotaxi service.

This may seem puzzling, but one of the biggest reasons seems to relate to a design issue of Cybercabs, according to a Fox News report. The Cybercab has neither LATCH nor ISOFIX child seat anchors. Given that some local laws around child seat requirements might call for such seats in a Cybercab, Tesla seems to have decided to cut out the issue altogether and ban anyone who might need a child seat in the vehicle.

Morningstar, Meanwhile, Approves

Tesla is planning another release event, noted a report from Morningstar, and that release event will feature the Tesla Roadster. The event is set to take place October 1, and will also give Tesla a brand-new "halo vehicle" to add to its lineup.

A "halo vehicle" is a high-end, high-performance luxury vehicle that is intended to show off exactly what a car company can do in terms of design and engineering. And Morningstar believes that the Roadster will serve as that vehicle for Tesla. In turn, this ultimately makes Tesla fairly valued, and Morningstar left its fair value estimate for Tesla shares at $450 per share.

Is Tesla a Buy, Hold or Sell?

data.title: Walmart Sets Out New Pharmacy Plan to Make Rural America Healthy Again
data.description:
Retail giant Walmart (WMT) is looking to strengthen its health services throughout rural America to plug a gap in national care shortages. The company said that over the next six months it will pilot a new Health Ambassador associate role at stores serving rural communities such as Lexington, TN; Caro, MI; Franklin, VA; Fort Scott, KS; and Searcy, AR.

Rural Health Ambassadors

At each store, a trained Walmart pharmacist who knows the community will serve as the Health Ambassador. Walmart said the Health Ambassadors will have "dedicated time to support customers beyond the pharmacy counter — understand their health goals and help connect them with relevant services and resources." The pilot will explore how more personalized, ongoing support can make it easier for rural customers to take the next step in their health journey.

Walmart said it has a unique opportunity to help make that support more practical, personal and connected to the way people already live. Approximately 90% of the U.S. population lives within 10 miles of a Walmart store or club, and 4,000 Walmart stores are located in medically underserved areas. Indeed, Walmart said that customers living in rural communities face healthcare provider shortages.

By giving pharmacists dedicated time to listen, coach and connect customers with relevant support, this pilot will help us learn how a familiar, trusted setting can make health resources more accessible, practical and actionable for people living in rural communities."

data.title: Western Digital Stock (WDC) Slips Despite Plans to Highlight AI Data Storage Needs at the AI Infrastructure Summit
data.description:
Western Digital (WDC) stock was down 2.75% on Tuesday, even after the company outlined plans to economically scale AI data storage in a new press release. The data storage company is set to highlight the growing need for storage as AI moves from testing into wider use. It also noted that the data created by AI keeps building over time. That makes the cost and scale of storage a main part of AI infrastructure.

Tim Rausch, senior vice president of HDD Development at Western Digital, will discuss how AI is changing storage needs and why scalable capacity is becoming a core part of AI systems at the AI Infrastructure Summit this week. Rausch's session will draw on a new IDC white paper sponsored by Western Digital.

What to Expect from the Western Digital Presentation

According to Western Digital, the report found that 61% of firms surveyed saw data growth of at least 25% over the past year due to AI. Additionally, 74% expect data volumes to grow by at least 25% over the next three years. Data lake volumes also grew over the past year, with 85.4% of firms reporting an increase.

Promotion

Rausch will outline Western Digital's view on how firms can manage the rising data load from AI. The talk will cover the need to balance storage capacity, speed, power use and cost as AI systems grow. It will also focus on new storage tools aimed at helping firms keep more data, gain more value from it and expand AI use at scale.

Rausch's presentation is set for September 16, 2026, at 3:50 p.m. on the main stage. Western Digital will also show its enterprise storage portfolio at booth No. 605 during the event. The demos will focus on storage for hyperscalers, cloud firms, neo clouds, and data center customers. The company says its systems are built to meet the capacity and power needs of large AI workloads. The AI Infrastructure Summit runs from September 15, 2026, through September 17, 2026, in Santa Clara, California.

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Down Today, 9/15/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are in the red on Tuesday, with the former down 0.46% and the latter off 0.44%. Equities are facing pressure from a rising 10-year Treasury yield, which is up 4.7 basis points to 5%, its highest level since 2007. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of owning stocks and also increase borrowing costs for companies. Furthermore, they reduce the present value of future cash flows. Elevated oil prices have supported yields in recent weeks, with Brent crude oil (BZ) up 2.5% to $108 per barrel.

Fed Decision Looms as Rate Hike Odds Remain High

Meanwhile, the Fed is set to announce its interest rate decision on Wednesday. Traders are pricing in 92.7% odds of a 25-basis-point hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Higher rates are generally viewed as a negative for stocks, as they tighten financial conditions and pressure stock valuations.

However, a rate hike may be necessary to support bringing inflation down to the Fed's 2% target. Last Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.4% year-over-year in August. The growth was driven by surging gasoline prices and a spike in wireless phone service prices.

data.title: SpaceX (SPCX) Exposure Becomes More Affordable With Morgan Stanley's New Stock Pick
data.description:
Satellite communications services provider EchoStar (SATS) is "an attractive entry point to get access to SpaceX (SPCX) at a discount." This is according to a team of analysts at Morgan Stanley (MS), led by Sean Diffley. Diffley kicked off coverage of ECHO with a Buy rating. He set a price target of $134, implying about 45% upside.

Diffley and his team backed their ratings with the following points, among others:

  • Discount 'Too Wide': EchoStar shares are currently down about 15% year-to-date to around $92 per share. Diffley believes SATS stock is trading at a discount that is "too wide to ignore."
  • Big Value from SpaceX Stake: In September last year, EchoStar agreed to sell its spectrum license to SpaceX in a roughly $17 billion deal. The arrangement includes up to $8.5 billion in cash and up to $8.5 billion in SpaceX shares. Diffley expects EchoStar to own about 2% or 262 million SpaceX shares when the deal closes in November next year. This is expected to fetch EchoStar almost $40 billion, compared to its current market cap of $27 billion.
  • Scarce Spectrum Asset: According to the Morgan Stanley team, EchoStar is one of the few publicly traded companies investors can turn to to get exposure to scarce spectrum. The team considers spectrum a scarce and appreciating asset class.
  • Potential DISH+DirectTV Merger: In 2024, EchoStar's efforts to merge its multi-channel TV service, DISH Networks, with rival DirecTV fell apart. However, Morgan Stanley still sees the merger option as positive for EchoStar.
  • Improving Credit Profile: According to Diffley, EchoStar's credit profile has improved significantly due to more spectrum sales. For example, the $23 billion deal with telco giant AT&T (T) helped EchoStar repay a key part of its debt. What's more, DISH DBS is being restructured to reduce debt. DBS runs DISH Network's satellite pay-TV business.

The analysts gave the rating despite flagging some of EchoStar's drawbacks. This includes several of EchoStar's assets being in bankruptcy.

What's more, EchoStar seems unlikely to issue a share buyback soon. This is despite the fact that the firm raised its authorized buybacks to $5 billion earlier in July.

Across Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on EchoStar's shares. This is based on six Buys issued over the past three months.

In addition, the average ECHO price target of $127.33 implies about 37% upside (see ECHO stock forecast here).

data.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad Author Robert Kiyosaki Says Biggest Stock Market Crash in History Has Started
data.description:
Rich Dad Poor Dad author Robert Kiyosaki declared that the largest stock and bond market crash in history has already begun. The author tied his latest warning to long-term forecasts from his 2002 book, stating that downturn signs are spreading out from Europe and Japan into world markets. Kiyosaki points to several factors, including high stock prices from artificial intelligence hype, war tension involving Iran, record global debt, and mass Baby Boomer retirements.

The author issued a clear warning to workers over age 40 holding traditional retirement accounts like 401(k) and IRA funds. Drawing a direct comparison to the Great Depression, which lasted from 1929 to 1954, Kiyosaki argued that major downturns destroy standard paper savings while opening massive buying opportunities for prepared investors.

Kiyosaki Is Urging Investors to Buy 'Safe-Haven' Assets Like Gold and Bitcoin

To prepare for market losses, Kiyosaki suggests leaving basic fiat savings behind. He still favors real estate that brings in money, oil wells, physical gold (CM:XAUUSD), silver, and Bitcoin (BTC-USD). Kiyosaki calls these safe-haven choices and digital assets key shields against government money printing (known as quantitative easing) when the economy falls.

data.title: OpenAI Partners with Anthropic and Google's DeepMind on AI Safety Measures
data.description:
OpenAI is joining forces with its rivals Anthropic and Google's (GOOGL) DeepMind to address artificial intelligence safety issues. The companies are increasing joint efforts to respond to growing public concern over economic and security risks from frontier AI models. Chris Lehane, global policy chief at OpenAI, noted that talks with Anthropic and Google DeepMind have been under way for several weeks.

Lehane noted that companies do not need a special trade pass to work together on basic safety rules. Comparing the plan to safety rules used by airlines, Lehane said airline firms often work together to protect people. Fear over big tech risks grew after Anthropic head Dario Amodei asked to slow down work on advanced models so teams can study potential dangers. Amodei's warning drew support from OpenAI chief Sam Altman and SpaceX's (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk. 

OpenAI Backs AI Safety Laws

While meeting with lawmakers in Washington, Lehane said OpenAI supports two-party plans to stop major AI dangers. OpenAI likes a national rule plan set up by Representative Jay Obernolte and Representative Lori Trahan. The company is also open to a Senate plan led by John Thune, Ted Cruz, and Amy Klobuchar to handle new tech risks.

Promotion

200% short exposure to META with METQ

Senator Jim Banks and Senator Adam Schiff also suggested a new law to help AI firms share warning signs. This rule would let tech companies warn each other about lost control over AI models and cyber attacks without breaking trade laws. However, lawmakers are running out of time before the House leaves Washington for the fall elections. With President Donald Trump speaking out against new AI limits and calling delay efforts a hoax, Congress is not expected to pass new AI safety laws this year.

Meta (META) trades near $667.65 with a Strong Buy rating and a $758.03 target, while Apple (AAPL) trades near $329.51 with a Moderate Buy rating.

data.title: Why Is Dell Stock Rising Today, Sept. 15?
data.description:

Kennedy said customers continue to place large orders for AI infrastructure. He also said some customers are now discussing supply needs several years into the future.

Dell's AI Server Orders Are Growing

Dell booked $6.1 billion in AI GPU server orders during fiscal Q2, matching the total booked over the previous three quarters combined. Over the past 12 months, Dell has recorded $13.2 billion in AI GPU server orders.

Dell also has more than 6,500 enterprise AI customers. That number has increased by more than 60% over the past six months.

data.title: Buy Coca-Cola Stock (KO) to Protect Against Market Volatility, Says UBS
data.description:
Beverage giant Coca-Cola (KO) can help safeguard a portfolio from market volatility, says UBS (UBS). The Swiss bank named its top stock picks that can help to insulate an investor's portfolio from increased volatility as bond yields rise and equity markets sink. And top of the list is Coca-Cola, which offers steady financial results in any type of market as well as a strong dividend payment.

UBS named KO stock its "top pick" in the beverage, household, and personal care category. The bank highlighted the company's quarterly dividend payment of $0.53 per share, giving the stock a healthy yield of 2.39%. In a note to clients, UBS acknowledged that Coke's share price has run nearly 30% this year, but said that the "premium relative to history is warranted given the degree of earnings visibility and upside."

Other Stocks to Buy Now

UBS's recommendation of Coca-Cola's stock comes with U.S. equity markets firmly in the red for September. All the major U.S. indices are firmly in the red on Sept. 15 as the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury rises above 5% and hits its highest level since 2007. At the same time, oil prices continue to rise, with Brent crude, the international standard, near $110 a barrel.
